'''{{PAGENAME}}''' enables the player to change data inside the game, such as current run data and game unlocks. '''{{PAGENAME}}''' can not change the Run History, these are stored in different files. The player may choose to edit the following two files:

*'''Logbook File''' stores your Single Player progress, basically everything that can be found inside the logbook.
*'''Run File''' stores information from your current run, such as what cards and artifacts the player has.

There are several reasons to why a Player would want to use make use of '''{{PAGENAME}}''' for the '''Logbook File''', some common ones are transferring data from a Steam or Gog account, restoring corrupted data, unlocking features such as all [[Covenant Ranks]] or resetting specific data, such as Mastered Cards or Win streaks. Whatever the reason may be, please always make a backup of your data before changing your '''Save File'''. If you want to reset your game progress completely, then you do not have to follow these steps and can instead reset your progress directly inside the setting of the game itself, in this case it is still advised to make a backup in case of regret.

Editing the '''Run File''' can be used for testing or cheating in Single Player. Note that it may be easier to install [https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2221577882 Stoker's deck editor] to do the same things with a better UI.

==Save File Location==

The '''Logbook File''' can be found in the following location that can either be navigated directly:

# '''Steam:''' C:\Users\USERNAME\AppData\LocalLow\Shiny Shoe\MonsterTrain
# '''Gog:''' C:\Users\USERNAME\AppData\LocalLow\Shiny Shoe\Monster Train\sync
# '''Game Pass:''' C:\Users\USERNAME\Appdata\Local\Packages\69C22bb6.MonsterTrain... \SystemAppData\wgs

or alternatively, the Player can search for %appdata% which directly leads to Roaming instead of the LocalLow folder and navigate to the directory from there. If you cannot find the file on a brand new game, you might want to start the game and tutorial once, so that the file gets created.

'''The Save Files''' (on Steam and Gog) inside the folder are then called

*'''Logbook File''':  metagameSave.json
*'''Run File''': saves\save-singlePlayer.json

On Game Pass, the save file is in a folder that is a combination of letters and numbers; it is not named clearly, as is the case for the other platforms. To find the correct file, first scroll down this page and find "Logbook File" and then click "Show complete logbook file." After you have this as a reference, go back to your file explorer, and start opening the files as text documents, any text editor should work. The file you are looking for is the one that is in the same format as the reference.

==Making a backup==

When changing data, always make a backup! For this, just copy the whole "Monster Train" folder onto your desktop or in a dedicated location. You copy the whole folder as you want to secure the Save File as well as any backup in case something goes wrong while editing your Files.

Tipp: If you often change your '''Save File''', because you use mods, share the computer with someone else or often reset data, it can be useful to have the Backup "Monster Train" folders just next to the original "Monster Train" folder inside the "Shiny Shoe" directory but renamed to a date, name of the other person, or Mods.

==Transferring Progress between Platforms (Steam, Gog, Game Pass)==

If you switch from one platform to the other and do not want to lose your progress, first make a Backup of your data as explained in the previous section. After you have done this, you can simply copy the metagameSave.json (Steam, Gog) file from one folder to the other and overwrite the file.

For Game Pass, open the file and copy the Plaintext instead, as the File name will be different to the other platforms.

==Restoring Corrupted Save Files==

If your Save File is corrupted, the easiest way to try to fix it is by using the backups of the Game itself. For this, follow the following steps:

# Backup of your data as explained in the previous section.
# Open metagameSave.json.1 with notepad or another text editor, and copy everything inside with Ctrl+A and Ctrl+C. Open metagameSave.json and overwrite everything inside with Ctrl+A and Ctrl+V.
# If this did not work, do the same with metagameSave.json.2, metagameSave.json.3 and so on until it does.

You should now have your data back from a earlier Game State.

==Editing Save File==

If instead of restoring an old game state, you want to edit a particular aspect of the File, you can go into the File and edit it manually. For this, first make a Backup!
